content.text:
I checked every claim in the overview against the record and found nothing to flag.

- **What happened:** "some shoppers' purchases" and the account of the cause match the record's plain-words lines. "Likely" stays on the cause, where the record puts it.
- **How it ended:** the rollback is in the list of what was done. It is confirmed and still in place, with automatic sync left off, as the record says. The fix is only a draft, so saying it has not been applied matches the record.
- **Figures:** {duration} and {customer_loss} are written in by code and weren't judged. The sentences around them still are, and the record supports them.

supported.quote: For {duration}, io-shop stopped confidently sorting some shoppers' purchases into categories.
rows: What a reader saw: The shop stopped confidently categorising many shoppers' purchases

supported.quote: The shop had switched to a newer model for this sorting.
That model only knows lowercase words, but the shop passed product titles to it without lowercasing them, which likely left capitalised words in those titles unrecognised.
Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: To end it, Argus rolled back the io-shop deployment. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off.
rows: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off

supported.quote: Argus has also proposed a fix, but it is only open as a draft and has not been applied.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #567 - opened as a draft
